filter_details.detail: Property explicitly marked as bug_bounty_scope='out-of-scope' and bug_bounty_eligible=false. KZG trusted setup parameter integrity (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) is an internal cryptographic assumption that cannot be exploited externally. The trusted setup is loaded at compile/init time and assumed correct by design.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are data column sidecars retained for MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS and served correctly via P2P?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS constant value and verify it matches specification requirements. 2. Review the sidecar storage implementation to verify retention period tracking logic. 3. Test that sidecars within the retention window are correctly served when requested via P2P. 4. Attempt to request sidecars at boundary conditions (exactly at MIN_EPOCHS, one epoch before expiry, one epoch after). 5. Verify that pruning logic only removes sidecars AFTER the full retention period has elapsed. 6. Test edge cases: clock skew scenarios, epoch boundary transitions, simultaneous prune and serve requests. 7. Attempt to force premature pruning through malicious P2P requests or timing attacks. 8. Verify the node does not crash or leak sensitive state when handling rapid sidecar requests near retention boundaries.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Specification Reference: Validator SG-007. This is a critical data availability invariant - premature pruning could cause validators to fail attestation duties or prevent peers from syncing correctly. The P2P entry point means an external attacker can probe the retention behavior.

checklist.title: Verify Sidecar Serving Behavior: Does the node correctly respond to P2P sidecar requests during the retention period?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Send valid P2P requests for data column sidecars that should be within the retention period. 2. Verify the node responds with the correct sidecar data. 3. Test requests for sidecars at various ages within the retention window. 4. Test requests for non-existent sidecars to verify proper error handling. 5. Test requests for sidecars just outside the retention period and verify appropriate denial/error response. 6. Check for information leakage in error responses that could reveal internal state. 7. Verify rate limiting and resource consumption for repeated sidecar requests.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Supporting check for boundary integrity. Focuses on the serving obligation during retention period.

checklist.title: Verify Pruning Logic: Is sidecar pruning correctly gated by retention period expiry?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review pruning code to identify all conditions that trigger sidecar deletion. 2. Verify the epoch calculation for retention period uses correct arithmetic (no off-by-one errors). 3. Test that pruning respects the MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS threshold precisely. 4. Attempt to falsify the invariant by: (a) triggering pruning during edge case scenarios (finality delays, reorgs), (b) testing with manipulated timestamps or epoch values, (c) concurrent pruning and serving operations. 5. Verify pruning is atomic or properly synchronized to prevent race conditions. 6. Check for integer overflow/underflow in epoch arithmetic that could cause premature pruning.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Internal logic verification. Attempts to falsify the invariant that pruning only occurs after retention period expires.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is blob data from the EL properly verified by CL before entering the polynomial commitment pipeline?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the code path where blob data is received from the EL via the Engine API (tb-004). 2. Verify that JWT authentication is properly enforced on all Engine API endpoints before processing blob data. 3. Locate the CL verification logic for blob data BEFORE it enters the polynomial commitment pipeline (cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction). 4. Check if blob data is validated for: (a) correct format/structure, (b) expected size constraints, (c) cryptographic integrity via KZG commitment verification. 5. Attempt to simulate a compromised EL scenario by injecting malformed or corrupted blob data and verify the CL rejects it. 6. Verify that any failure in blob verification prevents the data from reaching the KZG proof construction phase. 7. Check for any code paths that might bypass verification (e.g., fast paths, error recovery paths, cached data paths). 8. Test edge cases: empty blobs, oversized blobs, blobs with invalid BLS field elements.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Trust Boundary: tb-004 (EL-CL Engine API). This is a boundary property where data from the co-located EL crosses into the CL's polynomial commitment pipeline. The use of 'SHOULD' in the property description suggests verification may be optional or inconsistently applied - this is the key audit focus. Even with JWT authentication, a compromised EL (through separate vulnerability or malicious operator) could inject corrupted blobs if CL-side verification is missing.

checklist.title: Verify cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction has defense-in-depth against corrupted blob inputs
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction function/module (Validator-SG-002). 2. Identify all input parameters and their expected preconditions for blob data. 3. Verify that the function has defensive checks against corrupted blob data even if called directly (defense-in-depth). 4. Test with malformed inputs: (a) empty blobs, (b) truncated blobs, (c) blobs with invalid BLS field elements (values >= modulus), (d) blobs exceeding FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB limit. 5. Verify that KZG proof construction fails gracefully without producing invalid proofs. 6. Check that error conditions do not cause: (a) memory corruption, (b) infinite loops, (c) sensitive state leakage. 7. Verify that the function's behavior is deterministic - same input always produces same output or same error.
checklist.falsification_approach: To falsify this invariant: Attempt to construct valid-looking KZG proofs from corrupted blob data. If the function produces output (even invalid proofs) from corrupted input without explicit failure, or if it crashes/hangs, the invariant is violated.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Supporting check for boundary integrity. This verifies defense-in-depth: even if boundary verification at tb-004 fails, the internal polynomial commitment component should have its own validation. The cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction function should not blindly trust its inputs.

filtered_properties.description: The KZG trusted setup parameters (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) MUST be loaded from the canonical trusted setup and MUST NOT be modified at runtime. The integrity of these parameters is assumed by all KZG operations.
filtered_properties.filter_reason: Property is out-of-scope for bug bounty. The KZG trusted setup is a foundational cryptographic assumption - any compromise would require attacking the trusted setup ceremony itself, which is outside the scope of implementation security audits.
